bug_description.normalized: In vulnerable commit `9d20cd519ae62c8864ab237068e4c11490cbd0a9`, `compress_independent_block_mode` decodes the exact 45-byte staged witness through `FUZZ_dataProducer_preferences`, producing `prefs.compressionLevel = 7`, `prefs.autoFlush = 0`, `prefs.favorDecSpeed = 0`, and then leaving 17 bytes remaining for `compress_round_trip`. `compress_round_trip` allocates `uncompressedData = malloc(17)` and never initializes that heap buffer, yet it wraps the buffer in a second `FUZZ_dataProducer` and sets `uncompressedSize` to the full 17 bytes. `LZ4F_uncompressedUpdate` therefore treats the whole uninitialized region as an uncompressed block and copies it into `cctxPtr->tmpIn`. When the next `LZ4F_compressUpdate` switches back to compressed blocks, `LZ4F_flush` flushes that buffered block; because the active preferences are independent-block mode with HC level 7, `LZ4F_selectCompression` returns `LZ4F_compressBlockHC`, and `LZ4F_makeBlock` invokes that HC compressor on `tmpIn` before it later honors the uncompressed-block flag. `LZ4HC_InsertAndGetWiderMatch` then hashes `ip` through `LZ4HC_hashPtr(ip)`/`LZ4_read32(ip)`, which reads the first four bytes of the still-uninitialized heap data and matches the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. The fix removes the `malloc`ed fake uncompressed buffer entirely and instead uses a slice of the already-initialized fuzzer input as the uncompressed segment.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled fuzz bytes and materializes compression preferences used by the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly the 45-byte witness with SHA-256 `5543377f336a6398a6f5d7e58dfbd251c15aa30cb5784f505308ef96da0f20b6` and hex `0000000100000000001f0a0a0a0a0a0aff0a0a0a0a0aeef50a0a0a0a6c0100000a0a0a0a0a0a270a0a0a0afff0`. Under `FUZZ_dataProducer_*` semantics, seven `retrieve32` calls consume bytes at offsets 41, 37, 33, 29, 25, 21, and 17 with seeds `0x0a, 0x0a, 0x0a, 0x01, 0x0a, 0x0a, 0x0a`, yielding `prefs.compressionLevel = 7`, `prefs.autoFlush = 0`, `prefs.favorDecSpeed = 0`, and `prefs.blockChecksumFlag = 1`; 17 bytes remain afterward.

tainted_value_origin.description: After step 1 has consumed the preference bytes, this statement materializes the remaining attacker-controlled payload length `size = 17`, which later sizes both the uninitialized heap allocation and the claimed uncompressed segment length.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `LZ4HC_hashPtr(ip)` hashes the current `ip` by reading its first four bytes, so this lookup consumes the uninitialized bytes that were buffered from `uncompressedData`.
sink.note: The saved MSan trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `lib/lz4hc.c:268:18` with stack `LZ4HC_InsertAndGetWiderMatch -> LZ4HC_InsertAndFindBestMatch -> LZ4HC_compress_hashChain`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fuzz target allocates a heap buffer for the would-be uncompressed block with plain `malloc(size)` and never initializes it before later treating all `size` bytes as valid input to `LZ4F_uncompressedUpdate`.
root_cause.note: The staged fix removes this allocation and the fake producer built on top of it, replacing both with a slice of the already-initialized fuzzer input (`data + uncompressedOffset` .. `data + uncompressedEndOffset`).

parser_admitted.description: By this call the exact staged witness has already been decoded into `prefs` and `size`, a compression context exists, and the target is handing the logical uncompressed segment into the vulnerable LZ4 frame-compression path.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer target decodes the exact 45-byte witness into preferences (`compressionLevel = 7`, `autoFlush = 0`) and remaining size 17, then allocates `uncompressedData` with `malloc(17)` and treats all 17 bytes as a logical uncompressed segment without initializing them.

The uncompressed-update path records that the pending block is uncompressed and copies the 17 uninitialized bytes into `cctxPtr->tmpIn` because `autoFlush` is disabled and the block is smaller than the frame block size.

The next compressed update flushes `tmpIn`; level 7 plus independent blocks selects the HC compressor, and `LZ4F_makeBlock` calls that compressor on `tmpIn` before honoring the uncompressed-block flag.
HC compression hashes the first four bytes of the poisoned block through `LZ4HC_hashPtr(ip)`, and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at the hash-table lookup.

fine_trace.note: Source. This statement consumes the exact staged witness through `FUZZ_dataProducer_*` and materializes the compression settings that matter later: `prefs.compressionLevel = 7`, `prefs.autoFlush = 0`, `prefs.favorDecSpeed = 0`, and `prefs.blockChecksumFlag = 1`.

The target overwrites the parsed block mode to `LZ4F_blockIndependent`. That satisfies `LZ4F_uncompressedUpdate`'s independent-block requirement and later steers `LZ4F_selectCompression` toward `LZ4F_compressBlockHC` instead of the linked-block variant.
After step 1 has consumed the preference bytes, `producer->size` is 17. This length becomes both the heap-allocation size and the later claimed `uncompressedSize`.
Allocates a 17-byte heap buffer with indeterminate contents. No write initializes this region before later steps pass it into the frame compressor.

The target wraps `uncompressedData` in a second producer and immediately treats the full buffer length as valid payload. Because `FUZZ_dataProducer_remainingBytes()` only returns `producer->size`, `uncompressedSize` becomes 17 without any byte ever being written to `uncompressedData`.

fine_trace.code:
lz4Return = LZ4F_uncompressedUpdate(ctx, dst + compressedSize, dstCapacity,
                                      uncompressedData, uncompressedSize, NULL);
fine_trace.note: This project call hands the entire 17-byte uninitialized heap buffer to the frame writer as the next uncompressed block payload.
Inside the `LZ4F_uncompressedUpdate` invocation from step 6, `blockCompression` is `LZ4B_UNCOMPRESSED`, so the context records that the pending buffered block is uncompressed.

Because `prefs.autoFlush == 0` and the 17-byte input is smaller than the frame block size, the uncompressed-update path buffers the whole block in `tmpIn` instead of emitting it immediately. This `memcpy` is the MSan origin's "stored to memory at" site.

The later `LZ4F_compressUpdate` call at fuzz-target line 87 switches back to compressed blocks. Since step 7 left `cctxPtr->blockCompression` as uncompressed, this guard flushes the buffered `tmpIn` block before processing the new compressed input segment.
The flush path chooses the actual block compressor from the stored preferences. With `compressionLevel = 7` and independent blocks, `LZ4F_selectCompression` returns `LZ4F_compressBlockHC`.

fine_trace.code:
dstPtr += LZ4F_makeBlock(dstPtr,
                             cctxPtr->tmpIn, cctxPtr->tmpInSize,
                             compress, cctxPtr->lz4CtxPtr, cctxPtr->prefs.compressionLevel,
                             cctxPtr->cdict,
                             cctxPtr->prefs.frameInfo.blockChecksumFlag,
                             cctxPtr->blockCompression);
fine_trace.note: Flush passes the buffered 17-byte `tmpIn` block to `LZ4F_makeBlock` together with the HC compressor from step 10 and the still-uncompressed block flag from step 7.

Even though the block is logically uncompressed, `LZ4F_makeBlock` calls the non-null `compress` callback first. Here `src` is still `cctxPtr->tmpIn`, so the HC compressor receives the same 17 uninitialized bytes buffered in step 8.

Sink. The HC path reached from step 12 hashes `ip` with `LZ4HC_hashPtr(ip)`, which reads the first four bytes of the same block via `LZ4_read32(ip)`. Those bytes still come from the uninitialized heap allocation in step 4, so MSan reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this lookup.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan origin says the uninitialized bytes were created by the heap allocation at `compress_round_trip` line 47, which is the `malloc(size)` root-cause statement.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved MSan stack names the exact chain `compress_round_trip -> LZ4F_compressUpdate -> LZ4F_flush -> LZ4F_makeBlock -> LZ4F_compressBlockHC -> LZ4_compress_HC_extStateHC_fastReset -> LZ4HC_compress_generic_noDictCtx -> LZ4HC_compress_generic_internal -> LZ4HC_compress_hashChain -> LZ4HC_InsertAndFindBestMatch -> LZ4HC_InsertAndGetWiderMatch`, and fine steps 6-13 explain how the uninitialized heap buffer reaches that stack.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact witness-derived `prefs.compressionLevel = 7`, `prefs.autoFlush = 0`, and remaining `size = 17` cause the uninitialized 17-byte `uncompressedData` buffer to be buffered in `tmpIn`, flushed through the HC compressor, and finally hashed at the sink.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_48910 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `lib/lz4hc.c:268:18` while processing `poc`.

format.contract: Exactly the staged 45-byte file `gt_results/arvo_48910/poc` with SHA-256 `5543377f336a6398a6f5d7e58dfbd251c15aa30cb5784f505308ef96da0f20b6` and hex `0000000100000000001f0a0a0a0a0a0aff0a0a0a0a0aeef50a0a0a0a6c0100000a0a0a0a0a0a270a0a0a0afff0`. Under the vulnerable `FUZZ_dataProducer_*` semantics, this exact witness yields `prefs.compressionLevel = 7`, `prefs.autoFlush = 0`, `prefs.favorDecSpeed = 0`, and remaining `size = 17`; `compress_round_trip` then allocates `uncompressedData = malloc(17)`, treats all 17 bytes as a valid uncompressed segment without initialization, and the later compressed update flushes that buffered segment through the HC compressor. This Stage 02 trace does not generalize beyond the exact staged witness or prove which other byte sequences would decode to the same preference and size state.
